VERDICT: DISAGREE. Two defects in this PR's own added lines, both cheap to fix. Everything else I measured reproduces exactly as the PR body claims.

WHAT I RAN (branch head 4cc380e7fdc415fb7c5afeae38c296b31ab6a2e5, origin/main fetched fresh to bfe850796969980545811e1ffa551b9143965faf before any check):
- python -m pytest tests/ -q -> 522 passed, 1 pre-existing DeprecationWarning (tests/test_lwb_check_proof_reexecute.py:248). Matches the body.
- python scripts/lwb_check_proof.py -> exit 0, "lwb-proof check passed (21 record(s))".
- python scripts/lwb_check_proof.py --pr 41 --base bfe8507 --head 4cc380e -> exit 0 (the lwb-proof-pr shape CI runs).
- python scripts/lwb_check_proof.py --reexecute -> exit 0, "TOTAL: 24 of 147 commands re-executed, 0 uncomparable, 18 skipped-self, across 21 records -- ALL RE-EXECUTED COMMANDS MATCHED". Byte-for-byte the body's claim.
- python scripts/lwb_handoff.py --check -> exit 0, "passes all checks (2992 bytes)". Matches the body.
- python scripts/lwb_check_state_claims.py --repo . -> exit 0.
- python scripts/lwb_check_prefix.py, lwb_check_no_instruction_dep.py -> exit 0.
- python scripts/lwb_check_commit_identity.py --base bfe8507 --head 4cc380e -> exit 0.
- python scripts/lwb_lanes.py --base bfe8507 --head 4cc380e --pr-number 41 -> 8 FAILs, all "0 independent review(s) in reviews/41/". That is the only red I could reproduce locally, and GitHub's check-runs for 4cc380e show exactly one failing annotation in the `test` job (exit 1) with every other job green, consistent with the missing record being the sole blocker.
- git log -p bfe8507..HEAD | grep -ci [REDACTED, see the addendum at the end of these notes] -> 0. The private domain the body says was left behind on #32 is genuinely absent from this branch's history.

MUTATION PROBES (each reverted; working tree left clean, verified with git status):
1. Flipped proof/41.json's two corrected commands back to "verifiable": true (dropping verifiable_reason) -- i.e. deliberately re-introduced the exact overclaim this PR says it fixes. `--reexecute` then EXITS 1 with two errors: "self-referencing command is marked verifiable: true -- a proof record cannot claim its own re-execution as proof" and a digest mismatch on lwb_check_state_claims.py (recorded b46eda93..., re-run 9f0e1680...). The fix is real and its guard is NOT vacuous. NOTE, and this matters for how much the guard is worth: the CI step that runs it (`lwb-proof-reexecute`) is `continue-on-error: true` by design, so this guard reports and never blocks.
2. Edited HANDOFF.md's generated block from "21/21 proven" to "22/22 proven". `lwb_handoff.py --check` STILL PASSES (exit 0) -- it is a shape check only, so the PR body citing it as evidence proves less than it appears to. `lwb_check_state_claims.py --repo .` correctly FAILS: "stale deliverable proof state in generated block recorded=['22/22 proven'] re-derived=['21/21 proven']". The ordering trap is genuinely guarded here, and the generator IS the last commit on the branch (4cc380e), so the count is not stale.

FINDING 1 (blocking). reviews/27/dispatch-correction.md tells the reader to read evidence that this PR removes from the repository.
Lines added by 4b2d661/ddcdbc9, still present at head: "A green `lwb-lanes` here is not evidence that anything in this file was reviewed. Treat the review record under `reviews/32/` as the evidence, and read it."
Measured: `git ls-tree --name-only HEAD reviews/` lists 7,8,9,10,11,13,15-27 -- there is no reviews/32 on this branch. `git ls-tree -r --name-only origin/main reviews/32/` is empty -- there is none on main either. This PR's entire premise is that #32's six reviewer record-only commits (which is where reviews/32/ lived) are deliberately left behind; PR #32 is now closed unmerged (closed_at 2026-09-19T20:49:05Z, merged=false). So after this lands on main, the document's only named substitute for a mechanical review gate is a path that exists nowhere in the repository. scripts/lwb_check_state_claims.py's own docstring states the standard this violates, verbatim: "restated here in full rather than cited, so a reader never follows a pointer to vapour." A provenance-correction document should not ship a pointer to vapour.
Fix: one sentence -- either name #32's closed-PR review records by URL and say they are not in the tree, or say plainly that the supporting review records were dropped with the re-cut and what a reader should rely on instead.

FINDING 2 (blocking). HANDOFF.md's new item 3 hand-asserts PR state, two claims of which were already false when the commit was written, and the same edit deletes the line that forbade doing this.
Added text: "3. **IN FLIGHT.** #29 (runbook, routine specs, `.claude/` lane fix), #30 (plan + D21-D27 onto main), #31 (Actions merge path)." and "#32 itself is left open, commented as superseded, not closed by this session."
Measured via REST against commit authorship times (git log --format=%cI): the HANDOFF regeneration commits are b9c5b7c at 2026-09-19T20:22:38Z and 4cc380e at 2026-09-19T20:27:32Z.
  - #31: merged_at 2026-09-19T15:21:15Z -- MERGED five hours before the sentence calling it "IN FLIGHT" was written. False at authorship.
  - #30: closed_at 2026-09-19T17:06:52Z, merged=false -- CLOSED three hours before. False at authorship.
  - #29: closed_at 2026-09-19T20:49:09Z -- true at authorship, false now.
  - #32: closed_at 2026-09-19T20:49:05Z, merged=false -- "left open" was true at authorship, false now.
I want to be exact about which half of this is the author's error: #29 and #32 rotted after the commit and I do not charge those to this PR. #30 and #31 were already wrong when typed, and that is a directive 7a claim-of-project-state not backed by a command.
Compounding it, the same hunk DELETES the sentence that previously sat in item 1: "Branch tips and PR state are not written here; re-derive per `docs/handoff-protocol.md`." The replacement text then writes exactly the PR state that sentence prohibited.
Why no gate caught it: lwb_check_state_claims.py's VOLATILE_PATTERNS include `\bPR\s*#?\d+\s+is\s+(?:still\s+)?open\b` (line 338), which does not match "#32 itself is left open" (no literal "PR" token, "is left open" not "is open"), and nothing matches a bare "IN FLIGHT. #29 ... #30 ... #31". The script's own HONEST SCOPE docstring already concedes this class ("a claim that is stale but phrased without any of the covered patterns"), so this is a documented hole, not a regression in the gate -- but it does mean the green lwb-check-state-claims on this branch is not evidence these sentences are true.
Partial mitigation I checked before writing this, so it is on the record: docs/handoff-protocol.md section "The next session re-derives state, never trusts prose" says "The 'In flight' narrative is the *plan*; the command output is the *state*. Where they disagree, the commands win." That softens this to a narrative defect rather than a gate bypass. It does not make "IN FLIGHT: #31" true about a PR that merged at 15:21Z, in the one document the protocol tells every next session to read first.
Fix: drop the PR numbers from item 3, or restore the deleted "re-derive, do not write PR state here" line and keep item 3 to the non-volatile part (#32 is superseded by this re-cut; each open item needs proof + a record naming its current head).

NON-BLOCKING OBSERVATIONS (I would not hold the PR for any of these):
a. The PR body is stale against its own branch. It describes four cherry-picks plus "two new commits made in this recut" = six. The branch carries EIGHT: it also has 6805d150 ("rename proof/32.json to proof/41.json and re-declare its PR") and 4cc380e7 ("regenerate LAST after the proof/41.json rename"), neither mentioned. The body's Verification block was therefore measured at an earlier head; I re-measured every line of it at 4cc380e and they all still hold, so nothing is misstated, only unlisted.
b. proof/41.json's "commit" is "3509d2f", which is a commit on the abandoned #32 branch, not on this one. The equivalent commit here is ddcdbc9. It resolves today only through GitHub's retention of closed-PR refs; a fresh clone of main cannot resolve it. 6805d150's message states this choice deliberately ("the sha of the docs(reviews) commit this record proves, unaffected by which PR lands it"), and lwb_check_proof.py only shape-checks the field (COMMIT_RE), so this breaks no gate. NEAR-MISS I AM RECORDING RATHER THAN HIDING: my first pass concluded this sha did not exist at all, because `git cat-file -t 3509d2f` failed in my clone. That was my clone's fetch scope, not a defect in the record -- `gh api repos/.../commits/3509d2f` resolves it to 3509d2fd12ff37d6d4e9c5acef7716755eeca74a with the matching subject. I caught this before filing and would have made a false accusation otherwise.
c. proof/41.json acceptance_criteria[0] opens "THE FACT IS ESTABLISHED FROM EVIDENCE IN THE REPOSITORY, not from memory", but the two load-bearing facts -- the cron `23 * * * *` and the 13:59:25Z run-creation time -- appear nowhere in the repository except the document asserting them (grep for the cron and the trigger id across the tree hits only reviews/27/dispatch-correction.md and proof/41.json itself). The repository-visible corroboration I could actually verify is consistent but not conclusive: reviewer A's comment on #27 is timestamped 2026-09-19T14:09:46Z and #27 merged at 14:18:29Z, both confirmed by REST, which fits a 13:59 start but does not exclude a 13:23 cron fire. The record's own unproven[] says this honestly ("not anything the repository can check for itself"), so the disclosure is present and only the criterion's headline overclaims.

WHAT I VERIFIED IN THE DOCUMENT AND FOUND CORRECT (so this DISAGREE is not read as doubting the substance):
- reviews/27/cloud-reviewer.json really does carry reviewer_was_dispatched_by_author: false, reviewer_id reviewer-cloud-routine-buildcraft-01GaiKSWBCRLtcVa5fPYz4nQ-2026-09-19, verdict AGREE.
- The claim that a `true` value does NOT fail the gate is correct on all three cited grounds: _review_ok appends a notice at scripts/lwb_lanes.py:703-705 and falls through to `return str(reviewer_id)`; reviews/schema.json line 30 says verbatim "`true` does not fail the gate".
- "Ten mutation probes, two real findings, an explicit not-checked list" about #27's review is exact: the notes carry probes numbered 1-10, FINDING 1 and FINDING 2, and a NOT CHECKED section.
- The claim that a DISAGREE record blocks before staleness is checked is correct and I confirmed the code path: scripts/lwb_lanes.py:631 rejects verdict != AGREE and returns None BEFORE the reviewed_commit staleness branch at :653. This is why my own record below will keep lwb-lanes red until it is superseded -- see REMEDIATION.
- The env-leak gate is the GOOD shape, not the bad one: run without LWB_PRIVATE_NEEDLES it exits 1 with "UNCONFIGURED: ... a clean result proves nothing" rather than passing silently. My local red on that gate is my missing secret, not a defect in this PR, and I do not count it against the branch.

WHAT I DID NOT CHECK:
- Anything about the cron schedules `23 * * * *` and `53 * * * *`, the trigger id trig_01RcTdw6nbX2Tj9gFwmcZe8G, or the 13:59:25Z run-creation time. These are outside the repository and outside GitHub REST; I took them on trust and flag them as self-attested. I did not query any routine/trigger API -- out of scope for this reviewer.
- Whether the repository actually holds secrets named LWB_PRIVATE_NEEDLES and AUTO_TOKEN_QUEUE under those exact names. gh api repos/.../actions/secrets returns HTTP 403 through this proxy, so I could not confirm a misnamed secret would not silently expand to the empty string. Untested, and named here so it is not mistaken for a clean result.
- The Windows/macOS matrix. Everything above ran on ubuntu, Python 3.11.15. The lwb-portable and lwb-foreign-repo jobs are green on all three OSes on GitHub, which I read from check-runs rather than re-ran.
- I did not re-run the #27 review's own ten mutation probes; I verified only that they are present and counted as described.
- I did not review anything under plugins/, adapters/, or core/ -- this PR touches none of it (3 files: HANDOFF.md, proof/41.json, reviews/27/dispatch-correction.md).
- The MEASURED TRAP about plugins/*/lwb/bin/lwb_hook.py patching vendor/ vs core/ did not apply: no probe I ran touched either tree.

REMEDIATION PATH, stated plainly because a DISAGREE here is sticky. scripts/lwb_lanes.py checks verdict before staleness, so this record will keep reviews/41/ red even after the head moves. It is not unclearable by construction: this file has a stable name and this reviewer routine runs on a schedule, so a later run of reviewer B will re-read the branch and overwrite this same path with AGREE once Findings 1 and 2 are addressed. Both are one-sentence edits. I am not asking for a re-cut.
